passage: In the Monday review at the Gurugram office, Chandrika clicked to slide seven and said, "Our idea is a referral bonus for repeat clients." Sachin's coffee stopped halfway to his mouth. He had emailed that exact plan three weeks ago, with a costing sheet. His ears burned, and he wanted to say "that's mine" right there. He did not. Afterwards, in the pantry, he said quietly, "Chandrika, that idea was in my mail on the ninth. I would have liked a mention." She flushed and said she had "built on it." That evening Sachin printed the email trail and began sending weekly updates to the whole team in writing. He did not go to the manager yet. If it happened again, he would.

qa.q: When had Sachin emailed the referral bonus plan?
qa.a: Sachin emailed it on the ninth, three weeks earlier.

qa.q: What was Sachin feeling when Chandrika presented slide seven?
qa.a: Anger and a sense of being cheated: his ears burned and he wanted to say "that's mine."

qa.q: What could Sachin do if it happens again?
qa.a: Take the printed email trail and the written updates to the manager.

qa.q: How might Chandrika have felt when Sachin spoke to her in the pantry?
qa.a: She flushed and said she had "built on it," which suggests embarrassment or defensiveness.

grounding: A colleague presents the protagonist's idea as their own; he speaks privately, keeps records, moves to written updates and will escalate if repeated.

passage:
At the milk cooperative in Sojitra, Deepak had suggested moving the evening collection half an hour earlier so the milk stayed cooler on the tempo to the chilling plant. On Friday the secretary praised "Imran's clever timing plan" in front of the whole committee. Deepak's ears burned; Imran did not look at him.
After the meeting Deepak waited by the bicycles. "Imran bhai, that timing idea was mine. I told you by the weighing scale last Tuesday."
Imran rubbed his neck. "I thought we both came up with it."
"Then tell the secretary that. From now on I'm writing my ideas in the register book, with the date."
That evening Deepak wrote his next suggestion, cleaner cans for the morning round, in careful Gujarati, and signed it. If it happened again, he would take the register to the secretary himself.

qa.q: What was Deepak's suggestion about the evening collection?
qa.a: Moving it half an hour earlier so the milk stayed cooler on the tempo to the chilling plant.

qa.q: How did Deepak feel when the secretary praised Imran?
qa.a: He felt angry and cheated; his ears burned when his idea was credited to someone else.

qa.q: What will protect Deepak's ideas in future?
qa.a: Writing each suggestion in the register book with the date and his signature, and taking it to the secretary if the credit theft repeats.

qa.q: Why might Imran react by rubbing his neck?
qa.a: Imran likely feels awkward and caught, so he claims they both came up with it to save face.

grounding: A colleague takes credit for the protagonist's idea; he speaks to them privately, keeps written records and plans to go higher if it repeats.

passage:
The Thursday review at the Copenhagen studio ran long, and by the time Diego clicked to the last slide, Lars had stopped hearing the words. The slide showed the fold-flat bike rack Lars had sketched on a napkin at lunch two weeks ago, redrawn neatly, with Diego's initials in the corner. The client loved it.
Lars went to the kitchen and gripped the counter until his knuckles went pale. Then he found Diego by the coat hooks. "The bike rack was my sketch. You were at that lunch."
Diego frowned. "I developed it, though."
"You did the drawings, yes. The idea was mine. Next time, we credit both."
Back at his desk, Lars photographed the napkin and emailed it to himself with the date. He began posting his sketches in the team channel the day he made them. If it happened again, he would take it to Mette, the studio lead.

qa.q: What did the last slide show?
qa.a: The fold-flat bike rack Lars had sketched on a napkin, redrawn neatly with Diego's initials in the corner.

qa.q: What does Lars gripping the counter suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he is furious and hurt at seeing his idea claimed, and is calming himself before speaking to Diego.

qa.q: What went well in how Lars responded?
qa.a: He spoke to Diego privately and calmly, kept a dated record of the napkin, shared sketches openly, and planned to go to Mette only if it repeated.

qa.q: How might Diego see the situation?
qa.a: Diego seems to believe that doing the drawings earned the credit, so Lars's challenge may come as an unwelcome, defensive surprise.

grounding: A colleague presents the protagonist's idea as their own; he speaks privately first, keeps records, shares work openly, and will involve the lead if it repeats.
